findings.evidence: grep for `indCharacterSpanInt` across ./code returns only Spanning.lean definitions/lemmas plus one docstring mention in Artin.lean; grep for `indVirtualCharacters_eq_closure_indCharacter` returns only its own declaration and module docstring. Post-PR Artin.lean uses no declaration from Spanning.lean (its body cites `indVirtualCharacters`, `indClassFun`, `natCard_mul_indClassFun`, `mul_mem_indVirtualCharacters`, `isElementary_of_isCyclic`), yet now reaches Ideal.lean only transitively through Spanning.lean.
findings.fix: Split this strand into its own PR (it stands alone on merged material — `indVirtualCharacterSpanCyclic` exists on `main`), or drop it here and let the rewrite delete the displaced declarations. Keep this PR to the sharp identity, the direct-sum map, and the rational surjectivity.
findings.issue: Second topic bundled with the Artin work: `indCharacterSpanInt` and its four companion lemmas (lines 294-379) generalize the merged cyclic-only `indVirtualCharacterSpanCyclic` API to arbitrary families, and `indVirtualCharacters_eq_closure_indCharacter` (Ideal.lean:117) adds a second generating-set characterization. None of it is used by the new Artin proof or anywhere else in the repo, and it is what forces the new `public import ...Induction.Ideal` into Spanning.lean.

summary: Roadmap fit is clear: this proves both halves of the Layer 6 'Artin's induction theorem' item (README lines 395-400), and the direct-sum/base-change bundling is what the second half needs to be stated. But the PR also carries a severable second strand — the family-general `indCharacterSpanInt` development in Spanning.lean plus `indVirtualCharacters_eq_closure_indCharacter` in Ideal.lean — which nothing in the PR or the repo uses.
